text:
maria: Heads-up: console is flagging a spike in tenants with a 'compat-risk' indicator but the opt-out numbers look off. Some tenants show zero opt-outs even though they called the header. :thinking_face:

akash: Could be the same mismatch we saw where the legacy proxy emits `deprec_optout_v1` and the v2 router emits `deprec_optout_v2`. Console only reads v1 atm.

jess: That would explain it. Are both meters backed into the metrics pipeline?

akash: Yes, both land in graphite -> metrics-aggregator but with different metric names. Aggregation window is fine. The problem is consumer-side.

sam: Quick question: are there clients that set both headers and hit different codepaths so we double-count?

akash: Some clients do send both X-Client-Version and X-Compat. Router prefers X-Compat and increments v2 counter; legacy proxy increments v1 counter. No dedupe between them.

maria: For product/PM clarity we should show provisional counts that join both counters and a small note about possible duplication.

jess: Telemetry: can we create a temporary derived metric `platform.deprec.optout.prov` that sums both but tagged by path? That'll let console show breakdown.

akash: Yep. I can add a shim in the router to emit the canonical name and a tagging field `path=router|proxy` so we know the source.

sam: Also want an exemptions mechanism so tenants in migration programs don't get alerts. We need write-protected UI and audit logs.

maria: Proposal: tenant metadata gains `compat_exempt:true|false` and console shows an "Exempt" pill if true. Only console-admins can toggle and every toggle writes to audit-log service.

jess: For rollout UX, let's do: 1) console reads both counters and shows provisional badge + breakdown 2) add exemptions API + UI 3) switch to canonical metric and hide provisional after 7 days of stable readings.

akash: I prefer 10 days to be safe, but fine with a monitoring gate. I'll put a router PR to emit `platform.deprec.optout` (canonical) and add `path` tag. Short-term I'll emit the canonical name from both codepaths to simplify aggregation.

maria: Sam, can you mock the exempt pill? Designers want examples of the audit log entry too.

sam: Will do. Mock will show tenant id, actor, timestamp, and reason. Also add a small disclosure: "Counts provisional while we reconcile meters."

jess: On backfill: full retroactive backfill is heavy. Suggest we run a targeted ETL for tenants that currently have the provisional badge and show a quota anomaly. Backfill only those tenants' 30d window.

akash: Agreed. I'll provide log selectors and fields so infra can run the ETL. We'll tag results with `backfill:true` so console can surface that the numbers were backfilled.

maria: Ops: deploy-bot, can we canary the console change for 5% first?

deploy-bot: deploy initiated: console-feature-flags v2026.03.21-provisional -> canary (5%) :rocket:

maria: Timeline suggestion: probe canary today; exemptions API + UI in 4 business days; canonical metric switch after at least 7 days of stable signals and a targeted backfill run. If any red flags, escalate to #release-war-room.

jess: I'll open infra ticket for the ETL and tag you all. Also will add a small panel in console that shows sampling rate + last reconciliation time per-tenant. Helps PMs trust the badge.

akash: Note: make sure sampling window used by the aggregation is 1m to avoid mismatch with other dashboards.

sam: I'll include that in the mock. Anything else?

maria: Add a quick note to docs about the provisional status and how to request exemptions programmatically via API.

jess: Done, creating ticket now and will loop infra + security for audit retention rules.

maria: Thanks everyone. Let's reconvene if we see >10% discrepancy after canary. :+1:
